locator: ch. 1, unum esse Deum verum et vivum ... intellectu ac voluntate omnique perfectione infinitum: qui cum sit una singularis, simplex omnino et incommutabilis substantia spiritualis
interpretation: The council's confession of God's attributes (DS 3001): one, true, living, creator and lord, almighty, eternal, immense, incomprehensible, infinite in intellect, will and every perfection; one singular, altogether simple and unchangeable spiritual substance; really distinct from the world; most blessed; exalted above all. With 'bonitate sua' (DS 3002) for goodness. Kept as prose. It is the list that the definitional bridge STMT-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-SUFFICE abbreviates (owner decision on #143, 2026-10-24) and supports the five attributes not yet derived. As in the root (A), it states what the Church teaches; it is not used as a premise of the derivations.
